name: lattice-desktop-path-v1
description: Questions put to the shipped desktop chat path over synthetic-library-v3. Each item is one conversation of one to three turns; each turn carries a rubric (facts it must state, claims it must not make, documents it should cite, whether the honest answer is an abstention) and notes for the rubric judge. Tags say what an item is meant to exercise; the turn record says what actually ran. Scored by scripts/shipped_path_eval.py. The four rewrite and cross-turn tags were added on 2026-10-19 with the four items that cover them; runs before that date have the first 34 items only, and scripts/shipped_path_stats.py compare pairs runs on the items both have. The long-document tag and its twelve items were added on 2026-10-23 with the per-document cap cases (docs/design/2026-10-23-per-document-cap.md); runs before that date do not have them. Later on 2026-10-23 four long-document asks were rephrased as "everything the <document> records about <subject>" (lab-notebook, choir-minutes, conservation-record, observing-log), because their narrowing clause excluded a fact the rubric requires, and chronicle's ISO dates gained their written-out forms as alternates (docs/design/2026-10-23-answer-coverage.md section 7); runs before that are scored against the older wording.

tags.multi-hop: The answer needs facts from two or more documents.
tags.planner-rewrite: The question shares little vocabulary with the passage that answers it; the corpus planner's rewrite (or HyDE) is what reaches it.
tags.corrective-retry: A first pass is likely to come back thin (paraphrase, damaged scan, deep needle), so the sufficiency check may order the corrective retry.
tags.opening-or-section: The answer sits at a named document's opening, under a numbered clause, or deep inside one long document.
tags.abstain: The corpus does not contain the answer; a correct reply says so and invents nothing.
tags.conflict: Two documents (versions, rings, sessions) give different answers; a correct reply says which applies or that they differ.
tags.numeric-precision: A number, amount, date or identifier must come back exactly.
tags.follow-up-memory: A later turn only makes sense with the earlier turns of the same conversation.
tags.table: The answer is one cell of a Markdown table or CSV block.
tags.ocr: The answer is in an OCR-damaged scan.
tags.multilingual: The document is not in English.
tags.entity-collision: Several unrelated things share the name in the question.
tags.fragment: A one-line note beats long notes that only mention the topic.
tags.pronoun-follow-up: A later turn refers back with a pronoun or 'that'; its search query has to be rewritten with the antecedent, which may sit in an earlier answer rather than an earlier question.
tags.ellipsis-follow-up: A later turn is a fragment ('And on the edge ring?') that only becomes a question inside the earlier turn's frame.
tags.topic-shift: A later turn changes subject; carrying the earlier topic into its search query (rewrite drift) retrieves the wrong documents. Some return to the first topic past the intervening one.
tags.cross-turn-evidence: A later turn's answer needs facts established in two earlier turns, from different documents, put together.
tags.long-document: One long document holds six facts the answer needs, each in a different part of it, so retrieval has to bring back more than a few passages of the same document.

turns.ask: Go through the Saltings Cottage maintenance log and tell me everything it records about the Peallby stove.

rubric.notes: 'Saltings Cottage maintenance log' (household-log-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. 2025-03-19: the chimney sweep did the flue of the Peallby stove and left the certificate on the dresser. After the reline, the Peallby stove needs 36 hours of slow burning before the door seal stops weeping. Logs for the Peallby stove have to read under 41.6 per cent moisture on the meter, or the glass blackens within a day. The baffle plate in the Peallby stove cracked, and the replacement went in on 2026-10-14. The installer wants the Peallby stove serviced again within 71 weeks, whatever the glass looks like. A new carbon monoxide alarm went up beside the Peallby stove; it expires on 2030-11-26.

turns.ask: What did Councillor Reallhollow promise at the village hall trustees' open meeting? I want every commitment.

rubric.notes: 'Village hall trustees, open meeting, full transcript' (hall-transcript-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. I will have the roof survey back to the trustees by 2026-01-15, you have my word on that. While the library is shut I'll keep the hall open late on Thursdays, for the next 82 calendar days at least. I'm putting £6,497.92 from my ward budget towards the new kitchen, and that is settled. Youth groups will keep paying 66.6 per cent of the standard hire rate for as long as I'm on this committee. The ramp at the side door will be finished before 2026-03-18; I'll chase the builder myself. I'll give 58 hours a month to the repair cafe until we find a regular volunteer.

turns.ask: Pull together everything the Mill Lane chronicle records about Greassby Mill, in order.

rubric.notes: 'Mill Lane chronicle, compiled by the local history group' (chronicle-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. 1850-11-18. The wheel at Greassby Mill turned again for the first time since the flood, watched by most of the street. 1860-02-24. Greassby Mill was sold by the estate to the miller's family, and the deed was witnessed at the inn. After the weir upstream was lowered, the leat at Greassby Mill carried only 17.5 per cent of its old flow. Greassby Mill stood idle for 44 weeks while the millstones were re-dressed by a man brought in from the next county. The parish raised £4,525.32 by subscription to repair the roof of Greassby Mill after the gale. 1887-12-21. The last miller at Greassby Mill retired, and the building was let as a store.

turns.ask: List everything the soil lab notebook records about the Throassmere core.

rubric.notes: 'Soil laboratory notebook, autumn term' (lab-notebook-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. Moisture content of the Throassmere core after oven drying: 12.4 per cent. Median grain size in the lower band of the Throassmere core: 0.0127 mm, so silt rather than fine sand. Organic matter in the Throassmere core by loss on ignition: 57.5 per cent. The Throassmere core needed 15 hours in the oven before its mass stopped changing between weighings. Went back to the site of the Throassmere core on 2025-01-10 to take a second core, labelled with a B suffix. In the hydrometer test the fine fraction of the Throassmere core settled out at 0.0581 mm.

turns.ask: What have the family history notes established about Edith Fleastmere? Give me all the records.

rubric.notes: 'Family history research notes' (family-history-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. Baptism register: Edith Fleastmere was baptised on 1852-11-24 at the chapel on the hill. Passenger list: Edith Fleastmere sailed on 1870-12-15, travelling alone and listed as a seamstress. Her letters say the crossing took Edith Fleastmere 70 calendar days, most of it below deck. Probate: Edith Fleastmere left £4,680.83, divided equally between her two daughters. turns.ask: What does the apiary log record about the Slantgate hive across all the inspections?

rubric.notes: 'Apiary inspection log, home hives' (apiary-log-long) holds six facts about this, each in a different part of the document, and a full answer states all six. Queen seen in the Slantgate hive on 2028-09-14, marked yellow and laying well across five frames. Brood in the Slantgate hive covered 45.3 per cent of the frames checked, all of it capped and even. The Slantgate hive was treated for varroa; the strips stay in for 67 calendar days and then come out without fail. The Slantgate hive swarmed on 2034-05-20; the swarm was taken from the hedge and housed in the spare box. Honey from the supers on the Slantgate hive read 42.4 per cent moisture on the refractometer, dry enough to extract. The clearer board went on the Slantgate hive for 27 hours before the supers were lifted off.
